chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The hadith I hear from you — can I narrate it as being from your father? Or if I hear it from your father, can I narrate it as being from you?' He said: 'It is the same, except that your narrating it as being from my father is more beloved to me.'
And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Jamil: 'Whatever you hear from me, narrate it as being from my father.'

key_terms.أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ: More beloved to me — the Imam's personal preference, not a legal ruling
key_terms.أَرْوِيهِ: I narrate/transmit it — the technical act of transmitting hadith in the chain of narrators
key_terms.سَوَاءٌ: Equal, the same — affirming that the Imam's knowledge comes from a unified divine source

ai.seo_question: Can a hadith heard from Imam al-Sadiq be narrated as being from Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addressed a question that was deeply significant in early Shia hadith transmission: whether hadiths could be attributed interchangeably between him and his father Imam al-Baqir. The Imam confirmed their equivalence — reflecting the Shia theological principle that all Imams share a unified, divinely-transmitted knowledge — while expressing a personal preference for attribution to his father. This guidance encouraged scholars to refer hadiths back to earlier Imams in the chain, reinforcing the authority of the entire line of Imamate rather than a single individual.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The Hadeeth I hear from you<sup>asws</sup>, can I report it as being from your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, or I hear it from your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, can I report it as being from you<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is the same, except that you’re reporting it as being from my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> is more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup>’.

And Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said to Jameel (a narrator), ‘Whatever you hear it from me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, so report it as being from my<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> father<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’.
